overview: This file documents the regulation of printed material in occupied Japan through the case of Far East Photo Review, whose publisher sought authorization to distribute the bilingual illustrated magazine to occupation personnel and the Japanese public. State Department officials redirected the request to the War Department’s Reorientation Branch while privately doubting the publication’s suitability for reorientation purposes. The enclosed March 1947 issue—covering the 1946 Nankai earthquake, repatriation, economic and cultural life, overseas Japanese communities, and commercial advertising—provides a substantial example of the material under consideration. A later airgram reporting Nippon Times editor Kazuo Kawai’s criticism of inconsistent Occupation censorship broadens the file from one circulation decision to the larger tensions surrounding press control in postwar Japan.
interest: Combines a circulation request with the magazine, revealing Occupation reorientation criteria, Kawai's censorship criticism, and postwar Japanese community life.
